blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Bookkeeping, at the executive level, is the foundation on which every other financial conversation rests. A strategic decision built on weak bookkeeping is a house built on sand. A forecast, a valuation, a pricing model, a board report — all of them inherit the quality of the underlying entries. When the entries are reliable, every analytical layer above them becomes more valuable; when they are not, no dashboard, however pretty, can rescue the conversation.

The mistake many senior leaders make is to ignore bookkeeping because it feels too operational to be strategic. This is exactly backwards. The operational nature of the work is precisely what makes it strategic: the small daily choices made by a careful team determine, silently, what the company can prove about itself one, three, or ten years from now.

Respecting bookkeeping, funding it properly, and protecting its routines from cost cuts is one of the quieter signs of a serious finance leader. What looks like a clerical line item is in fact the ground everything above it stands on.

items.q: According to the text, what do a forecast, a valuation and a board report have in common?
options: They are all reviewed by the board
They all replace bookkeeping over time
They are all produced by the same team
They all inherit the quality of the underlying entries
items.why: "all of them inherit the quality of the underlying entries" — cada camada herda a qualidade dos lançamentos.

items.q: What does the image of "a house built on sand" convey?
options: That forecasts are always unreliable
That strategy resting on weak entries has no stable ground
That bookkeeping is expensive to maintain
That dashboards are more attractive than ledgers
items.why: A metáfora: decisão estratégica sobre uma base fraca não se sustenta.

items.q: Why do many senior leaders ignore bookkeeping, according to the author?
options: Because it is handled by external auditors
Because dashboards make it unnecessary
Because it is too costly
Because it feels too operational to be strategic
items.why: "they ignore bookkeeping because it feels too operational to be strategic".

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with which statement?
options: A polished dashboard can compensate for unreliable entries.
Small daily choices shape what a company can later prove about itself.
The operational nature of bookkeeping is what makes it strategic.
Protecting bookkeeping routines is a sign of a serious finance leader.
items.why: Inferência: o texto diz que nenhum dashboard, por mais bonito, salva lançamentos ruins.

items.q: The phrase "determine, silently, what the company can prove about itself" suggests that…
options: companies rarely need to prove anything about their finances
bookkeeping's consequences are invisible in the moment but decisive later
silence is the mark of a well-run finance function
the bookkeeping team should stay out of strategic discussions
items.why: Inferência: escolhas discretas hoje decidem, a prazo, o que a empresa consegue comprovar.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Emily defendendo o time de bookkeeping em uma revisão de custos. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
I understand the pressure we're all under, and I'm not going to pretend this line is untouchable. But before we sign off on cutting the bookkeeping team, I want the committee to picture where we'll be in three years.

Cutting here doesn't remove the work — it just moves it downstream, done less carefully, by people already stretched. Reconciliations slip. Entries get coded on a best guess. And none of that shows up in this quarter's numbers, which is exactly why it feels safe to cut.

Speaking as the person who signs the board report, I can tell you the report is only ever as good as the ledger beneath it. When the auditors arrive, or when we're valued in a fundraise, we won't be able to reconstruct what a careful team would have captured in real time. That gap is not recoverable after the fact.

So my recommendation is that we protect this function and find the savings elsewhere. It looks like a clerical cost today. It is, in fact, the ground every forecast and valuation we produce is standing on.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What does Emily say cutting the bookkeeping team actually does to the work?
options: It moves the work downstream, done less carefully
It automates the work through software
It transfers the work to the auditors
It eliminates the work entirely
items.why: "it just moves it downstream, done less carefully, by people already stretched".

items.q: Why does Emily say the cut "feels safe"?
options: Because the savings are guaranteed
Because the auditors have already approved it
Because the damage doesn't show up in this quarter's numbers
Because the team has volunteered to leave
items.why: "none of that shows up in this quarter's numbers, which is exactly why it feels safe to cut".

items.q: According to Emily, what happens when the auditors arrive or a fundraise valuation begins?
options: The bookkeeping team is rehired temporarily
They won't be able to reconstruct what wasn't captured in real time
The board report is automatically accepted
The company can quickly rebuild the missing records
items.why: "we won't be able to reconstruct what a careful team would have captured in real time. That gap is not recoverable."

items.q: What does Emily imply by mentioning that she is "the person who signs the board report"?
options: That the report is unaffected by bookkeeping quality
That she has the authority to block the cost review
That she has direct, first-hand stake in the ledger's reliability
That she prefers to delegate the decision
items.why: Inferência: ela fala de quem depende diretamente da qualidade do razão — não é opinião distante.

items.q: How would you best describe Emily's overall stance?
options: Indifferent to where the savings come from
Pragmatic — accepting cuts in general, but arguing this one is short-sighted
Purely emotional and defensive of her team
Reluctant to engage with the cost review at all
items.why: Inferência: ela reconhece a pressão de custos e propõe cortar em outro lugar — postura pragmática, não defensiva.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "Reliable bookkeeping is the foundation the whole finance function stands on." A foundation is…
options: a supervisory committee
a quarterly report
an external auditor
the base that everything else is built on
items.why: Foundation = fundação, a base sobre a qual o resto se apoia.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "Before the acquisition, the buyer commissioned an independent ___ of the target company."
options: reconciliation
dashboard
valuation
foundation
items.why: Valuation = avaliação do valor de uma empresa, típica em aquisições.

items.q: "Every forecast rests on the quality of the entries below it." To rest on something means to…
options: postpone it
audit it
depend on it for support
conflict with it
items.why: To rest on = apoiar-se em, depender de algo como base.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "The dashboard looked convincing, but the ___ entries feeding it were full of errors."
options: underlying
analytical
serious
operational
items.why: Underlying = subjacente: os lançamentos que estão por baixo, alimentando o painel.

items.q: Analytical layer is best understood as…
options: the physical filing system
the finance team's org chart
an interpretive level built on top of the raw data
the raw bookkeeping entries themselves
items.why: Camada analítica = o nível de análise construído sobre os dados brutos (forecast, valuation etc.).

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em revisões de custo e discussões de finanças. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The committee still has to sign off on the proposed cut." To sign off on means to…
options: formally approve
leak to the press
quietly ignore
audit line by line
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval.

items.q: "Cutting the team just moves the work downstream to people already stretched." This means the work is…
options: automated instantly
postponed indefinitely
eliminated completely
pushed onto others further along the process
items.why: Move downstream = empurrar a tarefa para etapas/pessoas seguintes no fluxo.

items.q: "The savings look real today, but they won't move the needle on our margins." This means they will…
options: trigger an audit
not make a noticeable difference
take years to calculate
double the workload
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, fazer diferença perceptível.

items.q: "Let's find the savings elsewhere and protect this function." Emily is proposing to…
options: cancel the cost review
look for the reductions in a different budget line
hire more bookkeepers
delay the board report
items.why: Find the savings elsewhere = obter a economia em outra rubrica, poupando esta.

items.q: "The team approved the reconciliation policy but never followed through on it." They…
options: carried it out to completion
rewrote it entirely
failed to carry it through in practice
escalated it to the board
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado; aqui, o oposto aconteceu.
